value.content:
Two threads each increment the same counter a million times in C. Why does the total fall short of two million?

The animation shows an illustrative lost update, a section protected by a mutex, and the indivisible increment performed by atomic_fetch_add. In C, the data race in the unprotected version has undefined behavior; the diagram is not an execution trace.

Measured on this machine: gcc 15.2.0, -O2 -pthread, Ryzen 7 5700U, 15 runs per version on November 1, 2026. Median times: no protection, 11.0 ms with an incorrect total; mutex, 92.2 ms; atomic, 21.4 ms. Mutex and atomic reached 2,000,000 in all 15 runs. These results apply to this program and environment, not a general performance rule.

Sources for the explanation:
C11/WG14 N1570, sections 5.1.2.4 and 7.17.7.5: https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1570.pdf
pthread_mutex_lock documentation: https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E19120-01/open.solaris/816-5137/sync-117/index.html
